familyConvention.observed: The coding folder family writes reads as resolver -> service, with no message, no handler and no twin spec.
familyConvention.houseLaw: CQRS. Counted in this app: 62 query folders carry a .query.ts and 64 carry a handler. The coding family is the outlier.
familyConvention.mirrored: the house law, by owner instruction
familyConvention.reversal: The first version of this record mirrored the local coding family and recorded the divergence as a finding. The owner overrode it. The finding stands; the new operation joins the law rather than the outlier.
familyConvention.notSettledHere: Converting the seven existing coding read operations to CQRS is a separate refactor of shipped, called code and belongs in its own record.

repairsOutsideBoundary.why: The API could not boot at all: submitCourseReview and updateCourseReview declare @Field(() => CourseReviewEntity) while the entity carried @Entity only - no @ObjectType, zero @Field. Nest refused to build the schema.
repairsOutsideBoundary.authorisedBy: the owner, explicitly, after the break was reported: 'lam di'
repairsOutsideBoundary.change: @ObjectType('CourseReview') plus @Field on the four scalars (courseId, userId, score, body). The course and user RELATIONS are deliberately left unexposed.
repairsOutsideBoundary.notOurs: This is another session's in-flight work; it is repaired here only because it blocked the live call.

findingsForOthers.observed: signInInit registers a session id in Redis (session:<userId> hash), but the token returned by signInVerifyOtp carries a DIFFERENT Keycloak sid. Every authenticated call with that token is then refused by SessionService.assertCurrent with SESSION_SUPERSEDED_EXCEPTION.
findingsForOthers.measured: registered sid ca74d075-...; token sid e08d750c-... for the same sign-in
findingsForOthers.notInvestigated: Out of scope for this feature. Reported rather than chased.
findingsForOthers.workaroundUsedForTheLiveCall: assertCurrent has an explicit branch - activeCount === 0 means there is nothing to enforce - so the test account's session hash was deleted before the call. Local dev Redis, one test account, session records only.
